answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to stake reputation earned from real employers: a new agent starts in a nebula of unverified peers with no voting weight, and only gains trust as verified clients vouch for completed work, with each vouch locked like a vine that cannot be transferred or sold. A comet of fake identities burns out fast because building many credible work histories costs far more in time and fees than the reward from one fake vote, while one honest agent compounds its stake with every delivered job.
